title: Introduction to a Function (Part 1)
description: What is a function? This video introduces the concept using real-world examples and ordered pairs.

title: Introduction to a Function (Part 2)
description: Continues the introduction to functions with more examples and the formal definition.

title: Introduction to Relations and Functions
description: Explains the difference between relations and functions with mapping notation examples.

title: Determine if a Relation is a Function
description: How to test whether a given relation qualifies as a function using ordered pairs and tables.

title: Determine if an Equation Represents a Function
description: How to determine if an equation defines a function by testing inputs for unique outputs.

title: The Vertical Line Test
description: Learn how to use the vertical line test to quickly determine if a graph represents a function.

title: Use the Vertical Line Test (Ex 1)
description: Worked example applying the vertical line test to determine if a graph is a function.

title: Use the Vertical Line Test (Ex 2)
description: Another worked example of the vertical line test with a different type of graph.

title: Determine if a Table of Values Represents a Function
description: How to check whether data in a table represents a function by examining x-values.

title: Introduction to Domain and Range
description: What are domain and range? This video covers the basics using ordered pairs, tables, and graphs. (Extension: domain, range and interval notation go beyond the FN1 CheckIt exercise.)

title: Find Domain and Range of Ordered Pairs
description: Practice finding domain and range from sets of ordered pairs and determining if the relation is a function. (Extension: the domain-and-range part goes beyond the FN1 CheckIt exercise; the function check is in scope.)

title: Determine the Domain of a Square Root Function
description: Step-by-step process for finding the domain when the function contains a square root. (Extension: domain, range and interval notation go beyond the FN1 CheckIt exercise.)

title: Determine the Domain of a Rational Function
description: How to find values that make a rational function undefined and write the domain. (Extension: domain, range and interval notation go beyond the FN1 CheckIt exercise.)

title: Domain: Square Root and Denominator Combined
description: Finding the domain when a function has BOTH a square root and a fraction — handling two restrictions at once. (Extension: domain, range and interval notation go beyond the FN1 CheckIt exercise.)

title: Interval Notation
description: How to read and write interval notation, including when to use parentheses vs. brackets. (Extension: domain, range and interval notation go beyond the FN1 CheckIt exercise.)

title: Set-Builder Notation
description: An alternative way to express domain and range using set-builder notation. (Extension: domain, range and interval notation go beyond the FN1 CheckIt exercise.)

title: Introduction to Function Notation (L9.2)
description: An introduction to function notation and how it's used to represent functions.

title: Function Notation
description: The basics of reading and writing function notation.

title: Evaluating Functions Using Function Notation (L9.3)
description: How to substitute a value into a function and evaluate the output.

title: Ex 1: Determine Function Values Given a Quadratic Function
description: Worked example evaluating a quadratic function at several input values.

title: Ex 1: Determine a Function Value From a Graph
description: How to read a function value directly off a graph.

title: Ex 2: Determine a Function Value From a Graph
description: A second worked example reading function values from a graph.

title: Ex: Given a Graph and a Function Value, Determine the Input (x-Value)
description: Working backward from an output to find the input using a graph — solving f(x) = value graphically.

title: Ex 1: Graph a Piecewise Defined Function
description: Extension (beyond the FN2 CheckIt exercise): how to graph a piecewise function by graphing each piece over its own interval.

title: Ex: Determine Function Values for a Piecewise Defined Function
description: Practice evaluating a piecewise function at different input values.

title: Ex 3: Determine a Function Value From a Piecewise Defined Graph
description: Reading function values from the graph of a piecewise function.

title: Ex: State the X and Y Intercepts Given the Graph of a Line
description: How to identify and state the x- and y-intercepts from a graph.

title: Ex 1: Determine the Domain and Range of the Graph of a Function
description: Reading domain and range directly from a graph and writing in interval notation.

title: Ex 2: Determine the Domain and Range of the Graph of a Function
description: A second worked example finding domain and range from a graph.

title: Given an Inequality, Graph and Give Interval Notation
description: A quick review of turning an inequality into interval notation, the skill you need before writing domain, range, and increasing/decreasing intervals from a graph.

title: Determine Where a Function is Increasing and Decreasing
description: How to identify increasing and decreasing intervals directly from a graph.

title: Determine if a Function is Increasing, Decreasing, or Constant
description: Practice classifying intervals of a graph, table, or set of ordered pairs as increasing, decreasing, or constant. (Constant intervals, tables, and ordered pairs go beyond the FN3 CheckIt exercise, which uses graphs only.)

title: Determine Key Characteristics of a Function Over a Closed Interval
description: Putting it all together: intercepts, domain/range, increasing/decreasing, and local max/min from one graph.

title: Ex: Increasing / Decreasing / Relative Extrema from Analyzing a Graph
description: Reads increasing and decreasing intervals and the relative (local) maximums and minimums from a graph, written as points.

title: Average Rate of Change (Introduction)
description: Defines average rate of change and works through examples of determining it from a function.

title: Find the Average Rate of Change Given a Function Rule
description: Worked example finding average rate of change starting from an equation.

title: Extension: Average Rate of Change on [3, 3+h]
description: Finding average rate of change on an interval that contains a variable — a preview of ideas that return in calculus.

title: Extension: Average Rate of Change Application: Hot Air Balloon
description: A real-world application finding the average rate of change of a rising hot air balloon's height over time.

title: Determine the Slope of a Line From a Graph (No Formula)
description: Finding slope visually using rise over run, without the algebraic formula.

title: Determine the Slope of a Line Given Two Points (Ex 1)
description: Using the slope formula to calculate slope from two given points.

title: Determine the Slope of a Line Given Two Points (Ex 2)
description: A second worked example applying the slope formula to two points.

title: Slope Given the Graph of a Line (Negative Slope)
description: Identifying a negative slope from a graph and understanding what the negative sign means about direction.

title: Slope of a Horizontal and Vertical Line
description: Why horizontal lines have a slope of zero and vertical lines have an undefined slope. (CheckIt's LF1 lines are never vertical; the slope-0 case can come up.)

title: Slope Given Two Points on a Horizontal and Vertical Line
description: Applying the slope formula to horizontal and vertical lines to see why the special cases arise algebraically. (CheckIt's LF1 lines are never vertical; the slope-0 case can come up.)

title: Rate and Slope
description: Connects slope and rate of change: why a line's rate of change is the same between any two points, and what that rate means.

title: Find the Equation of a Line Given Slope and a Point
description: Writing an equation in point-slope and slope-intercept form when given the slope and one point.

title: Find the Equation of a Line Given Two Points
description: Writing an equation in point-slope and slope-intercept form when given two points on the line.

title: Determine a Linear Equation Given Slope and a Point (Slope-Intercept Form)
description: A second worked example writing an equation directly in slope-intercept form.

title: Ex 1: Given Linear Equation in Standard Form, Write in Slope-Intercept Form to Graph
description: Rewrites a line in standard form Ax + By = C as y = mx + b to read off the slope and y-intercept, then graphs it.

title: Ex: Write a Linear Equation From Point Slope Form to Slope Intercept Form
description: Distributes and simplifies to turn a point-slope equation into slope-intercept form.

title: Graph a Line and Identify Slope and Intercepts (Fraction Slope)
description: Graphing a line from its equation and identifying the slope and intercepts, including with a fractional slope.

title: Find the Equation of a Line in Slope-Intercept Form Given the Graph
description: Working backward from a graph to write the line's equation in slope-intercept form.

title: Determine the x- and y-Intercepts of a Linear Equation
description: Finding the x- and y-intercepts algebraically from an equation in slope-intercept form.

title: Find the Slope of a Line From a Graph (Positive Slope)
description: Review (LF1): Reading slope directly from a graph using rise and run.

title: Graphing horizontal and vertical lines
description: Graphs x = c as a vertical line and y = c as a horizontal line, and explains why each looks the way it does.

title: Ex: Graph a Linear Equation in Point-Slope Form
description: Graphs a line from point-slope form by plotting the point and using the slope as rise over run.

title: Graph Linear Equations Given the Intercepts
description: Graphs a line by finding and plotting its x- and y-intercepts, then connecting them.

title: Savings Linear Function Application (Slope & Intercept Meaning)
description: A real-world savings example showing how to interpret slope and y-intercept in context.

title: Linear Equation Application: Cost of a Rental Car
description: Building a linear model from a word problem and using it to answer real-world questions.

title: Ex: Model the Balance of a Gift Card Using a Linear Function (m and b given)
description: Writes a decreasing linear model for a gift card balance and explains the slope and starting value in context.

title: Write a Quadratic Function in Vertex Form
description: Using formulas to write a given quadratic function in vertex form without completing the square.

title: Find the Vertex Form Given the Vertex and a Point
description: Extension (writing an equation from a vertex and a point goes beyond the PR1 CheckIt exercise, which gives you the function): Finding the equation of a quadratic function in vertex form given the vertex and one other point on the parabola.

title: Find a Quadratic Function Given the Vertex and Leading Coefficient
description: Extension (writing an equation from the vertex and a goes beyond the PR1 CheckIt exercise): Finding the equation of a quadratic function given the vertex and the value of a.

title: Graph a Quadratic Function Using a Table of Values
description: Graphing a quadratic function by completing a table of values.

title: Graph a Quadratic Function Using a Table of Values and the Vertex
description: Graphing a quadratic function by starting from the vertex and building a table of values around it.

title: Ex1: Write a Quadratic Function in Standard Form to Graph
description: Completes the square to rewrite a quadratic in vertex form a(x - h)^2 + k (this video calls vertex form "standard form"), then graphs it.

title: Quadratic Function: General Form to Vertex Form Using Vertex Equation (a=-2)
description: Finds the vertex of ax^2 + bx + c with h = -b/(2a) and k = f(h), then writes the function in vertex form.

title: Graphing a Quadratic Function in General Form: Vertex, Axis, Intercepts
description: Graphs a quadratic from ax^2 + bx + c by finding the vertex, the axis of symmetry, and the intercepts.

title: Factoring Application: Find the Time a Projectile Hits the Ground
description: Extension (the landing time goes beyond the PR2 CheckIt exercise, which asks for the maximum): Using factoring to find the x-intercepts (zeros) of a quadratic model, and interpreting what they mean in a projectile motion context.

title: Quadratic Equation App: Find The Time of Max Height, Max Height, and Landing Time of a Rocket
description: Uses the vertex of a projectile model to find when the rocket reaches its maximum height and what that height is, then when it lands.

title: Modeling Height with a Quadratic Function: Initial Height / Maximum Height
description: Reads the starting height and the maximum height from a quadratic height model, and explains what each coordinate of the vertex means.

title: Ex: Quadratic Function App: Maximize Area of a Rectangle with 3 Sides Fenced (Vertex)
description: Sets up an area model for a rectangle fenced on three sides and uses the vertex to find the dimensions that give the maximum area.

title: Find Sum, Difference, Product, and Quotient of Functions (Ex 1)
description: Four worked examples finding the sum, difference, product, and quotient of two functions, including the domain. (The domain part goes beyond the FN5 CheckIt exercise.)

title: Find Sum, Difference, Product, and Quotient of Functions (Ex 2)
description: A second set of worked examples combining functions arithmetically, including the domain. (The domain part goes beyond the FN5 CheckIt exercise.)

title: Determine f(g(x)) and g(f(x)) with Linear and Quadratic Functions
description: Finding both compositions of a linear and a quadratic function, showing why the order changes the result.

title: Evaluate Composite Functions Using Tables of Values
description: Extension (tables go beyond the FN5 CheckIt exercise): Four worked examples evaluating a composite function using tables of values for the two functions.

title: Evaluate Composite Functions from Graphs
description: Extension (graphs go beyond the FN5 CheckIt exercise): Four worked examples evaluating a composite function directly from the graphs of the two functions.

title: Determine Composite Function Values (Linear and Quadratic)
description: Evaluates compositions like f(g(3)) from the inside out: find the inner value first, then put it into the outer function.

title: Ex 1: Domain of a Composite Function - No Restrictions
description: Finds the domain of a composition f(g(x)) when neither function restricts the inputs.

title: Ex 2: Domain of a Composite Function
description: Finds the domain of a composition when the inner or outer function restricts the inputs, so f(g(x)) can be undefined at some x-values.

title: Function and Inverse Function Values
description: How to determine function values and inverse function values, reinforcing what f(x) and f⁻¹(x) each represent.

title: Find an Inverse Function From a Table
description: Finding an inverse function directly from a table of values, by swapping the input and output columns. (Extension: inverses from tables go beyond the FN6 CheckIt exercise.)

title: Function and Inverse Function Values Using a Table
description: Determining function values and inverse function values using a table of values. (Extension: tables go beyond the FN6 CheckIt exercise.)

title: Find Inverse Function Values Without Finding the Inverse Function
description: A shortcut for finding a specific inverse function value without first solving for the entire inverse function. (Extension: finding single inverse values goes beyond the FN6 CheckIt exercise, which asks for the inverse formula.)

title: Determine if Two Functions Are Inverses
description: Testing whether two given functions are inverses of each other by checking both compositions.

title: Ex 1: Determine if the Graph of a Relation is a One-to-One Function
description: Uses the horizontal line test to decide whether a graph is one-to-one, and so whether the function has an inverse.

title: Lesson: Inverse Functions
description: A lesson on what an inverse function is, why it swaps inputs and outputs, and why only one-to-one functions have inverses.

title: Ex 1: Find the Inverse of a Function
description: Finds an inverse by writing y = f(x), swapping x and y, and solving for y.

title: Ex: Find the Inverse of a Rational Function
description: Finds the inverse of a rational function by swapping x and y, clearing the fraction, collecting the y terms, and factoring out y.

title: Ex: Restrict the Domain to Make a Function 1 to 1, Then Find the Inverse
description: Restricts the domain so a function becomes one-to-one, then finds its inverse and states the inverse's domain and range.

title: Function Transformations: Horizontal and Vertical Stretches and Compressions
description: Explains how a and b affect the graph of a*f(b(x-c))+d, covering stretches and compressions in both directions together. (Extension: stretches and compressions go beyond the FN4 CheckIt exercise.)

title: Graph a Transformation of a Line Segment: g(x)=-af(x+c)+d
description: Worked example applying a full set of combined transformations — reflection, stretch, and both shifts — to a simple line segment. (The stretch factor a goes beyond the FN4 CheckIt exercise; the reflection and both shifts are exactly what CheckIt asks.)

title: Graphing Multiple Function Transformations (Part 1 of 2)
description: How to graph a function in the form y = a·f(b(x+c))+d by applying each transformation in the correct order. (The stretch and compression steps go beyond the FN4 CheckIt exercise.)

title: Write a Function Rule in Terms of f(x) — Vertical Stretch & Shifts (Ex 1)
description: Writing the equation of a transformed function described in words, involving a vertical stretch and shifts in both directions. (Extension: the vertical stretch goes beyond the FN4 CheckIt exercise.)

title: Write a Function Rule in Terms of f(x) — Horizontal Stretch & Reflection (Ex 2)
description: A second worked example writing a transformed function's equation, this time involving a horizontal stretch and a reflection. (Extension: horizontal stretches and reflections across the y-axis go beyond the FN4 CheckIt exercise.)

title: Transformation: Graph |f(x)|, Given f(x)
description: How to graph the absolute value of a function from its original graph — any part below the x-axis reflects upward. (Extension: |f(x)| is beyond the FN4 CheckIt exercise.)

title: Matching Transformations of the Basic Rational Function
description: Matching a transformed graph of a rational function to its correct equation, reinforcing stretch/compression and reflection recognition. (Extension: rational functions come later; matching their transformations goes beyond the FN4 CheckIt exercise.)

title: Function Transformations: Horizontal and Vertical Translations
description: Shifts a graph up, down, left, and right, and shows why f(x - h) moves the graph right even though there is a minus sign.

title: Function Transformations: Reflections Across the x-axis and y-axis
description: Reflects a graph across the x-axis with -f(x) and across the y-axis with f(-x), and compares what each does to the points.

title: Functions Transformations: A Summary
description: Summarizes shifts, reflections, stretches, and compressions in one place, with how each shows up in the equation.

title: Graphing Multiple Function Transformations - Part 2 of 2
description: Graphs functions with several transformations applied, in order, by moving key points one step at a time.

title: Angles in Standard Position
description: An introduction to drawing and identifying angles in standard position.

title: Plot Positive Angles in Degrees in Standard Position and Convert to Radians
description: Sketching a positive angle given in degrees, then converting it to radians.

title: Plot Negative Angles in Degrees in Standard Position and Convert to Radians
description: Sketching a negative (clockwise) angle given in degrees, then converting it to radians. (Extension: negative angles go beyond the TR1 CheckIt exercise.)

title: Plot Positive Angles in Radians in Standard Position and Convert to Degrees
description: Sketching a positive angle given in radians, then converting it to degrees.

title: Plot Negative Angles in Radians in Standard Position and Convert to Degrees
description: Sketching a negative angle given in radians, then converting it to degrees. (Extension: negative angles go beyond the TR1 CheckIt exercise.)

title: Radian Measure
description: An introduction to the radian as a unit of angle measure, built from arc length and radius.

title: Converting Angles in Degree Measure to Radian Measure
description: Worked examples converting angles from degrees to radians.

title: Convert Angles in Radian Measure to Degree Measure
description: Worked examples converting angles from radians to degrees.

title: Determine Positive and Negative Coterminal Angles
description: Worked examples finding coterminal angles in degrees, both larger and smaller than the original angle.

title: Determining Coterminal Angles in Radian Measure
description: Finding coterminal angles when the original angle is given in radians.

title: Arc Length and Area of a Sector
description: An overview of the arc length and sector area formulas, in both degrees and radians, with worked examples.

title: Determine the Reference Angle for a Given Angle
description: Worked examples finding the reference angle for angles sketched in standard position, across all four quadrants.

title: Find Sine, Cosine, and Tangent Values for 120 Degrees
description: Using a reference triangle and the unit circle to find sine, cosine, and tangent for an angle in Quadrant II.

title: Find 6 Trig Function Values of 210 Degrees
description: Finding all six trig function values — sine, cosine, tangent, cosecant, secant, and cotangent — for one angle in Quadrant III.

title: Determine Exact Trig Function Values With the Angle in Radians
description: Finding exact trig function values using the unit circle when the angle is given in radians instead of degrees.

title: Properties of Trig Functions: Domain, Range, and Sign in Each Quadrant
description: An overview of how each trig function's sign changes across the four quadrants — the reasoning behind the ASTC pattern.

title: Determine the Quadrant of the Terminal Side Given Trig Function Signs
description: Working backward: given the signs of two trig functions, determine which quadrant the angle must be in.

title: Determine Reference Angles of Angles Between 0 and 360 Degrees
description: More practice finding reference angles across all four quadrants in degrees.

title: Determine Reference Angles of Angles Given in Radians
description: Practice finding reference angles when the angle is given in radians, including negative angles.

title: Find Trigonometric Function Values for 0 Degrees or 0 Radians
description: Finding exact trig values for a quadrantal angle (on an axis rather than inside a quadrant) — a useful edge case.

title: Determine Trigonometric Function Values Using the Unit Circle
description: Reading trig function values directly from coordinates on the unit circle.

title: Find Sine, Cosine, and Tangent Values for 225 Degrees
description: A worked example in Quadrant III, pairing with the existing 120° (QII) and 210° (QIII) examples for broader quadrant coverage.

title: Animation: Graphing the Sine Function Using the Unit Circle
description: An animation showing exactly how the sine wave is traced out as a point moves around the unit circle.

title: Animation: Graphing the Cosine Function Using the Unit Circle
description: The same animation approach applied to cosine, showing how it traces out from the unit circle's x-coordinate.

title: Amplitude and Period of Sine and Cosine
description: How to determine the amplitude and period of sine and cosine functions, and how the graph changes as each one changes.

title: Exploring Transformations of Sine and Cosine: y = A sin(Bx-C)+D with Desmos
description: An interactive exploration showing how A, B, C, and D each affect the graph of a sine or cosine function.

title: Determine if a Table Represents a Linear or Exponential Function (Ex 1)
description: Checking differences vs. ratios to determine whether a table of values is linear or exponential.

title: Determine if a Table Represents a Linear or Exponential Function (Fractions/Decimals)
description: A second worked example, including tables with fractional or decimal common ratios.

title: Determine if a Table Represents a Linear or Exponential Function
description: Another worked example distinguishing linear from exponential tables of values.

title: Determine Exponential Function Values and Graph the Function
description: Evaluating an exponential function at given inputs and using those values to graph it.

title: Evaluate a Given Exponential Function to Predict a Future Population
description: A real-world application evaluating an exponential growth model to make a future prediction.

title: Determine a Continuous Exponential Decay Function and Make a Prediction
description: Building and evaluating an exponential decay function, including base e, in a real-world context.

title: Exponential Model: Determine Age Using Carbon-14 and Half-Life
description: A classic exponential decay application — using a half-life model to estimate age.

title: Graph Exponential Functions
description: A full worked example finding domain, range, and horizontal asymptote for a transformed exponential function involving base e.

title: Find the Equation of a Transformed Exponential Function From a Graph
description: Working backward from a graph — reading the shifts and reflections to write the equation of a transformed exponential function.

title: Equations of a Transformed Exponential Function (4 Examples)
description: Four worked examples determining the equation of a transformed exponential function from given transformation information.

title: Match the Graphs of Translated Exponential Functions to Equations
description: Practice matching transformed exponential graphs to their correct equations, reinforcing shift and asymptote recognition.

title: Write Logarithmic Equations as Exponential Equations
description: Worked examples converting logarithmic equations into their equivalent exponential form.

title: Write Exponential Equations as Logarithmic Equations
description: Worked examples converting exponential equations into their equivalent logarithmic form.

title: Evaluate Logarithms Without a Calculator — Whole Numbers
description: Evaluating logarithms by inspection, asking what exponent produces the given argument.

title: Evaluate Common Logarithms Without a Calculator
description: Evaluating common (base 10) logarithms by inspection and writing the result as an exponential equation.

title: Evaluate Common Logarithms on a Calculator
description: Using a calculator to evaluate common logarithms that don't come out to a clean whole number.

title: Evaluate Natural Logarithms on the Calculator
description: Using a calculator's LN key to evaluate natural logarithms.

title: Graph an Exponential Function and Logarithmic Function
description: Graphing an exponential function and its logarithmic inverse together, showing the mirror-image relationship across y = x.

title: Vertical Asymptotes and Domain of Logarithmic Functions
description: Determining the domain and vertical asymptote of a logarithmic function, verified graphically.

title: Domain, Range, and Asymptote of y = -ln(x-6)
description: A worked example finding domain, range, and vertical asymptote for a transformed natural logarithm involving a horizontal shift and reflection.

title: Domain, Range, and Asymptote of y = -log₃(x)+4
description: A worked example finding domain, range, and vertical asymptote for a transformed logarithm involving a vertical shift and reflection.

title: Expand Logarithmic Expressions (Ex 1)
description: Using the properties of logarithms to expand a logarithmic expression as much as possible.

title: Expand a Logarithm Containing a Radical
description: Expanding a logarithmic expression that contains a radical, using the power property to handle the fractional exponent.

title: Solve an Exponential Equation Using Logarithms
description: Solving an exponential equation by taking the logarithm of both sides and using the power property to isolate the variable.

title: Solve an Exponential Equation with Logarithms — Variable on Both Sides
description: Solving an exponential equation where the variable appears in exponents on both sides of the equation.

title: Solve a Basic Exponential Equation with Base Ten Using the Logarithm Definition
description: Solving an exponential equation by rewriting it in logarithmic form using the definition from EL3.

title: Solve a Basic Exponential Equation with Base e Using the Logarithm Definition
description: Solving a base-e exponential equation using the natural logarithm and the log/exponential definition.

title: Solve a Basic Logarithmic Equation by Writing It in Exponential Form
description: Solving a logarithmic equation by converting it to exponential form and solving algebraically.

title: Exponential Growth Function: Population, Base e
description: Building and evaluating a continuous population growth model using base e.

title: Evaluate a Given Exponential Function to Predict a Future Population
description: Evaluating an exponential growth model to make a future population prediction.

title: Compounded Interest Problems: Solving for Time
description: Solving compound interest problems for the time variable, including using a graphing calculator's time-value-of-money solver.

title: Graph a Transformation of the Tangent Function (Period and Horizontal Shift)
description: Finding the period and horizontal shift of a transformed tangent function, then graphing it.

title: Graphing a Transformation of the Cotangent Function
description: Graphing a cotangent function with a different period and a vertical stretch.

title: Determine the Key Characteristics and Graph a Transformation of the Secant Function
description: Finding all key characteristics — domain, range, period, and asymptotes — of a transformed secant function, then graphing one full period.

title: Graphing a Transformation of the Cosecant Function
description: Describing and graphing a transformation of the cosecant function.

title: Evaluate Basic Inverse Trig Expressions Involving Arcsine Using the Unit Circle
description: Evaluating arcsine expressions at special angle values using the unit circle, with answers checked on a graphing calculator.

title: PF3 Video Walkthrough: Inverse Trigonometric Functions
description: Dr. Romero's narrated walkthrough of inverse sine, cosine, and tangent: finding exact values from the unit circle, staying inside each function's range, and sketching the three graphs.

title: Solve a Right Triangle Using Inverse Trigonometric Functions
description: Using inverse trig functions and a calculator to find a missing angle when two sides of a right triangle are known. (Extension: calculator and triangle work go beyond the PF3 CheckIt exercise.)

title: Evaluate a Trig Expression with an Inverse Trig Function in Terms of u
description: Evaluating a composition of a trig function and an inverse trig function where the answer is expressed in terms of a variable u. (Extension: compositions go beyond the PF3 CheckIt exercise.)

title: Solve a Right Triangle Given an Angle and the Hypotenuse
description: Solving a right triangle given one angle and the hypotenuse, finding both missing sides and the second acute angle.

title: The Law of Sines: The Basics
description: An introduction to the Law of Sines and how to use it to solve a triangle, before tackling the Ambiguous Case.

title: The Law of Sines — No Solution (SSA)
description: Explains how the Ambiguous Case can produce no valid triangle at all (beyond the TE5 CheckIt exercise: CheckIt's two-sides-and-an-angle problems always have one or two triangles).

title: The Law of Sines — Two Solutions (SSA)
description: Solving a triangle using the Law of Sines when the Ambiguous Case produces two valid solutions.

title: Use the Law of Cosines to Find the Measure of an Angle of a Triangle (SSS)
description: Finding a missing angle of a triangle using the Law of Cosines when all three sides are known.

title: Find Height of Building Using Angle of Elevation and Angle of Depression
description: Using right triangle trigonometry to find a building's height from an angle of elevation and an angle of depression. Finding a height goes beyond the TE6 CheckIt exercise, but the angle setup is the same.

title: Use the Law of Sines to Determine a Side Length (AAS)
description: Finding a missing side with the Law of Sines when two angles and a side are known — the same setup as the lighthouse problem.

title: Determine an Unknown Length Using the Law of Sines (Example 1)
description: An application of the Law of Sines to find an unknown length.

title: Determine an Unknown Length Using the Law of Sines (Example 2)
description: A second application of the Law of Sines to find an unknown length.

title: Use the Law of Cosines to Find the Measure of an Angle of a Triangle (SSS)
description: Finding an angle with the Law of Cosines when all three sides are known — the first step in the campers problem.

title: Ferris Wheel Trigonometry Problem
description: Extension (beyond the TE6 CheckIt exercise): finding the equation that models a rider's height on a Ferris wheel, then using it to find the height and the times at a specific height.

title: Sum and Difference Identities for Cosine
description: Developing and using the sum and difference identities for cosine. CheckIt also asks for sines; the sine formulas work the same way (faq-4).

title: Double Angle Identities
description: The double-angle identities for sine, cosine, and tangent, and how to use them. (Extension: the TE1 CheckIt exercise doesn't ask for double angles, but the power-reducing formulas come from these.) (This is the updated version linked from the original Mathispower4u video.)

title: Half Angle Identities
description: The half-angle identities and how to choose the sign from the quadrant.

title: Simplify Trigonometric Expressions (Sum of Fractions: sine and cosine)
description: Adding fractions and using identities to simplify a trig expression — the same moves as cos θ + sin θ tan θ = sec θ.

title: Simplify Trigonometric Expressions (Sum of Fractions: sec and tan)
description: Combining fractions with secant and tangent using a common denominator and identities.

title: Verifying Identities: Sum, Difference, Double, and Half Angle Identities
description: Extension (beyond the TE2 CheckIt exercise): Verifying identities when the sum, difference, double-angle, or half-angle formulas are needed.

title: Find an Angle That Shows an Equation Is Not an Identity (sine and cosine)
description: Beyond the TE2 CheckIt exercise: Using a single counterexample angle to show an equation is not an identity.

title: Find an Angle That Shows an Equation Is Not an Identity (csc and cot)
description: Beyond the TE2 CheckIt exercise: A second counterexample example, this time with cosecant and cotangent.

title: Solve Trig Equation by Factoring: 2sin²(x) − sin(x) − 1 = 0 (Radians)
description: Solving a quadratic-in-form trig equation by factoring, then finding solutions with the unit circle. (Extension: factoring goes beyond the TE3 CheckIt exercise.)

title: Solve a Trig Equation with a Double Angle: sin(2x) (Radians)
description: Solving a double-angle equation using substitution and the unit circle — the same method as sin(2θ) = 1/2.

title: Solving a Trig Equation with a Multiple Angle (Radians)
description: A second worked example solving an equation with a multiple angle using substitution.

title: Find the Correct Graph for a Polynomial Function Using Intercepts, Zeros, and End Behavior: Factored
description: Putting the pieces together: using a factored polynomial's zeros, intercepts, and end behavior to decide what its graph looks like, the same reasoning as the sketch in the PR3 CheckIt exercise.

title: Degree, Leading Term, and Leading Coefficient of a Polynomial Function
description: Identifying the degree, leading term, and leading coefficient of a polynomial function, the inputs needed to predict end behavior. (When a polynomial is a product of linear factors, add their exponents to get the degree.)

title: Summary of End Behavior of Polynomial Functions
description: A shortcut summary for determining the end (long-run) behavior of a polynomial function from its degree and leading coefficient.

title: Determine the Zeros/Roots and Multiplicity From a Graph of a Polynomial
description: Extension (reading a graph goes beyond the PR3 CheckIt exercise, which gives the formula): Reading a polynomial's zeros and their multiplicities directly from its graph, based on whether it crosses or touches the x-axis.

title: Polynomial Long Division: Degree 4 Divided by Degree 2
description: Extension (a degree 4 dividend goes beyond the PR4 CheckIt exercise, which divides a degree 3 polynomial by a degree 2 one; the loop is the same): A worked example of polynomial long division, dividing a degree-4 polynomial by a degree-2 polynomial.

title: Use the Remainder Theorem to Determine if a Binomial Is a Factor of a Polynomial
description: Using the Remainder Theorem to test whether a binomial like (x-a) is a factor of a given polynomial.

title: Ex: The Rational Root (Zero) Theorem
description: An example of listing the possible rational roots of a polynomial function using the Rational Root Theorem.

title: Solve Basic Rational Equations
description: An introduction to solving rational equations by clearing the denominators and checking for excluded values.

title: Solve Rational Equations with Like Denominators
description: Solving a rational equation where the denominators already match, a simpler special case of clearing fractions.

title: Solve a Rational Equation with No Solution: x/(3x-9) - 6 = 1/(x-3)
description: A worked example where clearing the fractions produces a candidate that turns out to be an excluded value, leaving no solution, the same situation as the FAQs on checking candidates and on no-solution equations. (Extension: equations with no solution go beyond the PR6 CheckIt exercise.)

title: The Domain of Rational Functions
description: Finding the domain of a rational function by identifying where the denominator equals zero.

title: Determining Horizontal and Vertical Asymptotes of Rational Functions
description: Finding both horizontal and vertical asymptotes of a rational function from its equation.

title: Determine Domain, Holes, and Asymptotes of a Rational Function
description: A full worked example finding the domain, any holes, and the vertical and horizontal asymptotes of a rational function together.

title: Solve a Quadratic Inequality: Factorable (Greater Than or Equal to Zero)
description: Solving a factorable quadratic inequality using boundary points and a sign chart, with the solution checked graphically.

title: Extension: Solve a Quadratic Inequality — No Solution
description: A quadratic inequality where no value of x satisfies the inequality — the sign chart never produces the sign being asked for. This goes beyond the PR8 CheckIt exercise, whose quadratics always cross zero twice.

title: Extension: Solve a Quadratic Inequality — All Real Numbers
description: A quadratic inequality satisfied by every real number — the sign chart shows the desired sign in every region. This goes beyond the PR8 CheckIt exercise, whose quadratics always cross zero twice.

title: Solving Rational Inequalities
description: A lesson on how to solve rational inequalities using critical points, a sign chart, and interval notation.

title: Ex 2: Solving Rational Inequalities
description: A second worked example solving a rational inequality, with the solution verified graphically.
